sources.claim: I-16 is ranked the 3rd deadliest highway in Georgia
sources.value: REFUTED / unsourced. NHTSA FARS 2020-2024, Georgia (STATE 13), crashes whose TWAY_ID or TWAY_ID2 names the route: I-75 342 fatal crashes/394 deaths; I-20 223/253; I-85 194/205 (undercount: 'I-75/85' rows credited to I-75 only); I-285 152/162; I-95 74/87; I-16 61/66 (by year 13, 16, 12, 16, 9 deaths). I-16 is 6th among Georgia interstates by deaths, and lowest of the six per mile (~0.08 deaths/mile/yr vs 0.16 I-95, 0.22 I-75, 0.51 I-285, using FHWA route-log lengths). US and state routes not ranked, so it is not 3rd of all highways either way. The only '3rd' sources found are law-firm pages citing a 'Secure Life' list (a home-security marketing site), i.e. marketing; no GDOT/GOHS/NHTSA ranking. Drop.
sources.verified_how: Computed locally from the already-downloaded FARS accident files acc2020-acc2024.csv (scratchpad/fresh/run-3553/fars/): STATE=13, regex I-<n> over TWAY_ID|TWAY_ID2, sum FATALS. ROUTE=1 TWAY_ID spellings checked (I-16, 'I-16 EB', 'I-16 W' all captured). Chatham-only I-16 (14 crashes/14 deaths) and I-95 (23/26) carried from facts-4538. URL curl -sIL 200.

sources.claim: roughly 30,000 truck trips daily through Chatham County (I-16 carrying the majority)
sources.value: UNSOURCED -> replace. No GPA, GDOT or CORE MPO source gives 30,000. GPA: the Port of Savannah handles 14,000 to 16,000 truck moves a day, Monday through Friday (2025, per GPA release reported by WTOC 2026-01-27). The CORE MPO Regional Freight Plan (2023) gives ~7 million trucks moving through the region in 2019 (about 19,000/day averaged over a year) and gives no I-16 share. GPA routes much port traffic to I-95 via Jimmy DeLoach Parkway (facts-4715), so 'I-16 carrying the majority' is also unsupported.
sources.verified_how: curl 200; page text contains '14,000 to 16,000 truck moves daily, Monday through Friday'. gaports.com returns 403 to curl and a Cloudflare challenge in Chrome (not solved), so the GPA figure is cited through WTOC; corroborated by https://container-news.com/port-of-savannah-posts-second-busiest-year-on-record-in-2025/ (200). CORE RFTP: https://www.thempc.org/docs/lit/CoreMpo/Plans/FreightTransportation/2023/Dec/Task2/CORE%20RFTP_Goods%20Mvmt%20Assessment_Final_10302023.pdf (200, pdftotext searched).

replacements.old_exact: Interstate 16 connects Savannah to Macon across 167 miles of Central Georgia — and it has earned the nickname "The Devil's Highway" for good reason. Ranked the 3rd deadliest highway in Georgia, I-16 carries the bulk of freight from the Port of Savannah, the fastest-growing container port on the U.S. East Coast.
replacements.new_text: Interstate 16 connects Savannah to Macon across about 166 miles of Central Georgia. It is a main truck route for freight from the Port of Savannah, the fastest-growing container port on the U.S. East Coast, and federal crash data recorded 66 deaths on I-16 statewide from 2020 through 2024 (NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System).
replacements.note: Length per FHWA route log (165.71 mi). Drops nickname and '3rd deadliest'. 'carries the bulk of freight' softened to 'a main truck route' (GPA routes much I-95 traffic over Jimmy DeLoach Parkway - facts-4715). 'Fastest-growing ... East Coast' is GPA's own description; kept.

replacements.old_exact: I-16 earned this nickname because it is the 3rd deadliest highway in Georgia. The combination of heavy Port of Savannah freight traffic (30,000+ truck trips daily through Chatham County), active construction zones, two-lane rural stretches, and high-speed travel produces a steady stream of fatal crashes — particularly involving tractor-trailers.
replacements.new_text: I-16 is a main truck route for Port of Savannah freight, and the port handles 14,000 to 16,000 truck moves a day, Monday through Friday (Georgia Ports Authority). Heavy tractor-trailer traffic, GDOT construction at the I-16/I-95 interchange, long rural stretches with two lanes in each direction and high speeds all add risk. Federal crash data recorded 61 fatal crashes and 66 deaths on I-16 across Georgia from 2020 through 2024 (NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System).
replacements.note: Publishes as FAQPage structured data. Every number sourced (GPA via WTOC; FARS computed). 16@95 construction per facts-4538/1793.

outOfScopeFlags: Title 'Savannah's Deadliest Freight Corridor' is a superlative contradicted by FARS (I-95 deadlier in Chatham) - owner retitle.
'Every container that leaves the port by road travels I-16 westbound' (body and FAQ 1) is false - GPA routes I-95 traffic via Jimmy DeLoach Parkway (facts-4715).
'5.9 million TEUs in 2023' (body, FAQ 1): 5.9M was the 2022 record; CY2025 ~5.7M, FY2026 5.67M (facts-4715) - stale/wrong year.
'Georgia's truck fatalities rose 81% from 2013 to 2023 (142 to 257)' not checked.
